title: Microsoft Teams: meeting policy setting for profanity filtering in transcripts
summary: Pass: the filtering default, organiser-policy behaviour, rollout facts and documented controls are supported. Licensing should acknowledge the general Teams licence requirement, and the checklist should not prescribe policy-assignment controls missing from the table. The changed release notes do not change the transcript-filtering guidance.

claims.claim: Teams adds a meeting policy controlling profanity masking in live and saved meeting transcripts.
claims.quote: Teams administrators will be able to use a meeting policy to control whether profane words are masked in live transcription and saved meeting transcripts.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationales
claims.claim: Filtering is on by default and preserves existing masking behaviour unless an administrator changes the assigned policy.
claims.quote: The setting will be on by default, preserving the current transcript-masking behavior unless an administrator changes the assigned policy.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Disabling filtering allows previously masked words to appear in both live and saved transcripts.
claims.quote: When an organizer is assigned a policy that turns filtering off, profane words can appear without masking in both the live and saved transcript

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The meeting organiser's assigned meeting policy determines transcript-filtering behaviour.
claims.quote: The meeting organizer's assigned policy determines the behavior for the meeting.

claims.claim: The filtering-off behaviour applies to the assigned organiser's scheduled meetings.
claims.quote: words that would otherwise be masked can appear in both the live and saved transcript for that organizer's scheduled meetings.

claims.claim: The filter is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting settings > Recording and transcription > Filter out profane words in live transcription.
claims.quote: A new Filter out profane words in live transcription setting will be available in the applicable Teams meeting policy under Meeting settings > Recording and transcription.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy uses -Identity and -FilterProfanityInTranscript with Enabled or Disabled to set transcript profanity filtering.
claims.quote:
### -FilterProfanityInTranscript
Controls whether meeting transcripts filter profanity.
Possible values are:
- **Enabled**: Filters profanity from the meeting transcript.
- **Disabled**: Does not filter profanity from the meeting transcript.

claims.quote: This feature has not been fully released yet, so the setting will have no effect.

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference gives Enabled as the FilterProfanityInTranscript default.
claims.quote:
### -FilterProfanityInTranscript
Controls whether meeting transcripts filter profanity.
Default value: | Enabled

claims.claim: Transcription is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Transcription.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to **Meetings** > **Meeting policies**.
2. Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one.
3. Toggle **Transcription** **On** or **Off**.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTranscription $true or $false controls whether transcription is allowed.
claims.quote:
To manage meeting transcription using PowerShell, use the **`-AllowTranscription`** parameter in Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy.
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "Your Policy Name" -AllowTranscription $true

claims.claim: The existing Transcription policy setting allows or prevents transcription rather than choosing profanity masking.
claims.quote: Transcription is both a per-organizer and per-user policy setting. For meetings and events to include transcripts, the organizer must have this setting turned on. The user who starts the recording or transcript must also have this setting turned on.

claims.claim: No administrator UI or API controlling each participant's live-caption profanity preference is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams profanity admin captions policy. Read meeting-transcription-captions, teams-admin release notes and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; controls found concern caption availability or transcript filtering, not each participant's profanity preference.

claims.claim: No organiser-level or per-meeting override surface for transcript profanity filtering is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: FilterProfanityInTranscript override; Teams transcript FilterProfanityInTranscript tenant master switch organizer override. Read Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy, meeting-transcription-captions and MC1478003; the notice explicitly rules out organiser and per-meeting overrides.

claims.claim: The Teams release notes say users can update their live-caption profanity preference in settings.
claims.quote: Users who have already set their preference will keep their current setting. As a result, some users may begin seeing unfiltered profanity in live captions by default after this rollout. Users can update this preference in settings at any time.

claims.claim: Meeting transcripts are stored together with recordings in OneDrive and SharePoint storage.
claims.quote: Transcripts are stored together with meeting recordings in OneDrive and SharePoint storage.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions

claims.quote: Searched: Teams Copilot masked transcript profanity. Read copilot-teams-transcription, meeting-transcription-captions, teams-admin and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; no downstream masking rule for this setting found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because no licence specific to this setting is published.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Replace the licensing notes and opening licensing paragraph with: 'Teams requires a Teams licence for each user in the organisation, except for joining meetings anonymously. Microsoft has not published a licence requirement specific to this filtering setting.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access in sources and retain only the feature-specific licensing gap in the cost rationale and Open questions.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends confirming the business need and reviewing compliance policies and transcript requirements before disabling filtering.
claims.quote: Before turning filtering off, confirm the business need and review whether the change aligns with your organization's compliance policies and transcript requirements.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends updating internal transcript guidance if the organisation changes default policy behaviour.
claims.quote: Update internal transcript guidance if your organization changes the default policy behavior.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Global meeting policy supplies the default for users without an existing policy assignment, and custom policies can be assigned to selected users.
claims.quote: To apply changes to all users in your organization who don't have an existing policy assignment, use the **Global policy**. To exclude certain users from the global policy, create and assign a custom meeting policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Meeting policies can be assigned to users or groups using the transcription page's assignment steps.
claims.quote: To specific users: Select your policy, select Manage users > Assign users ... To groups: Select the Group policy assignment tab, select Add, enter the group name, select the policy name, and then select Apply.

claims.claim: No separate tenant-wide transcript profanity-filtering master switch is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams profanity tenant switch; Teams transcript FilterProfanityInTranscript tenant master switch organizer override. Read Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy, meeting-transcription-captions and MC1478003; found the organiser's meeting policy, not a separate master switch.

claims.claim: The Learn pages do not give the new filter's admin-center path at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams transcript FilterProfanityInTranscript tenant master switch organizer override; Teams profanity admin captions policy. Read meeting-transcription-captions, teams-admin and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; the filter's UI location is supplied by MC1478003, not these Learn pages.

claims.claim: The role documentation names general meeting-policy administrators rather than a role specific to this filtering setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams transcript profanity filtering license pricing FilterProfanityInTranscript; Teams profanity admin captions policy. Read using-admin-roles and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; the roles cover meeting policies generally and no filter-specific role is named.

claims.claim: The change is a masking control over transcript text, rather than a feature that autonomously performs actions.
claims.quote: Teams administrators will be able to use a meeting policy to control whether profane words are masked in live transcription and saved meeting transcripts.

claims.claim: Users whose organiser retains filtering on are not affected by the new setting.
claims.quote:
Who is not affected
- Users whose meeting organizer is assigned a policy that keeps filtering on.

claims.claim: Meeting policies can be reached through Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to **Meetings** > **Meeting policies**.
